settings.heading: Built around what neutralizes — not what plugs.

settings.text: Three things do the work. Coconut oil, baking soda and organic jojoba. The jojoba is what makes it soak in instead of sitting on your skin.

settings.title: Organic Virgin Coconut Oil
settings.text: The base. Cold-pressed and unrefined, so it keeps everything a lab would take out. Refined coconut oil is cheaper and always the same, but getting it that way strips out most of what makes the oil worth using.

settings.title: Organic Jojoba
settings.text: The carrier oil. Jojoba is close to the oil your own skin makes, so it soaks in instead of leaving a film on top. Mineral oil and petroleum jelly are much cheaper and always the same, but they sit on the surface. Jojoba is the closest plant match to your own skin oil we know of.

settings.title: Baking Soda
settings.text: The baking soda. Aluminum-free, food-grade, at a measured amount. Some commercial baking sodas include aluminum-based anti-caking agents, which we do not want anywhere near your skin. We pay more for the aluminum-free kind.

We started Real Skin Care because our family wanted products where every ingredient was something we could confirm. Conventional deodorants gave us a choice between aluminum compounds that plug sweat ducts and "natural" sticks that failed by lunch or burned skin we love.

So we built this one around what works, respects the skin, and lists every drop on the label.

— Sean Fillmore

• No aluminum, in any form
  • No preservatives you'd need to look up
  • No parabens
  • No synthetic fragrance
  • No talc
  • No synthetic thickeners

settings.heading: Is this an antiperspirant?
settings.row_content: No. Antiperspirants use aluminum compounds (chlorohydrate or zirconium) to plug sweat ducts, which is how they stop perspiration. We leave aluminum out, so this will not reduce how much you sweat. It works on odor instead. Sweat is a body function, not a defect, and we are working on the smell side of it.

settings.heading: Will this irritate skin that reacts to baking soda?
settings.row_content: It might. Some people react to baking soda even at moderate amounts, and we use a measured amount because it does real work on odor. We recommend a patch test on the inner arm for a few days before daily underarm use. If you have reacted to baking soda deodorants before, start there.

settings.heading: Why is it a roll-on instead of a stick?
settings.row_content: Sticks need hardeners and glide agents — usually propylene glycol or synthetic waxes — to hold that solid form. We didn't want those in the formula. The roll-on goes on a little wetter than a stick, so give it a moment to absorb before dressing. The trade-off is honest: less convenient format, cleaner ingredient list.

settings.heading: Why does the texture change with the temperature?
settings.row_content: Cold-pressed virgin coconut oil firms below 76°F and softens above it. That is what real, unrefined coconut oil does. Refined coconut oil stays uniform year-round because the lab strips out the variation, along with most of what makes the oil worth using. If the bottle feels firm, roll it in your hand for ten seconds before use.

settings.heading: How long does the odor protection last?
settings.row_content: Most customers get a full day from a single morning application. If you're highly active, in a hot climate, or transitioning from an antiperspirant (your microbiome adjusts over the first two to four weeks), you may want to reapply midday. This isn't a 48-hour clinical-strength claim; it's a real formula doing real work for the length of a normal day.

settings.heading: What's the difference between the scent variations?
settings.row_content: The base formula is identical. Only the essential oil blend changes. Geranium Flower is floral with cedarwood and patchouli grounding. Calming Lavender pairs lavender with lemon and rosemary. Mountain Cedarwood is the most woodsy of the four — cedarwood-forward with geranium and patchouli. Wildcrafted Frankincense is the quietest, just frankincense and sandalwood. All use named organic essential oils, never synthetic fragrance.

settings.heading: I'm switching from a conventional antiperspirant. What should I expect?
settings.row_content: The first two to four weeks are an adjustment period. Your underarm microbiome rebalances after years of aluminum-plugged ducts, and you may notice more sweat or stronger odor temporarily — that's the transition, not the formula failing. Most customers find it settles by week three or four. A patch test the first few days is still smart, especially if you've had skin reactions to other deodorants.
